item.title: AWS Agent Registry Introduces Custom Metadata Schemas for Structured Governance
item.description:
AWS Agent Registry Introduces Custom Metadata Schemas for Structured Governance

Custom metadata schemas are now available in AWS Agent Registry. This update allows administrators to define a set of organization-specific key-value pairs that registry records must carry, enabling structured validation, discovery, and governance.

🔍 Overview

AWS Agent Registry provides a catalog to register, approve, and discover resources and custom records. Each record within the registry carries a name, a description, a protocol descriptor, and an approval status. With the introduction of custom metadata schemas, administrators can enforce structured metadata on every record to maintain consistency across teams.

⚙️ How it works

A custom metadata schema is a set of organization-defined key-value pairs. The registry administrator defines the schema—including field names, types, allowed values, and whether each field is required or optional—and applies it to the registry.

Key behaviors of the schema validation include:

  • Supported Field Types: Each field can be configured as Text, Enum, URL, or Boolean.
  • Scope of Fields: The schema has common attributes that apply to every record type, and administrators can add dedicated fields that only apply to specific record types.
  • Enforcement and Validation: When a record is created or updated, AWS Agent Registry validates the custom metadata against the schema. If a record includes an unknown field, a missing required field, or an invalid value, it is rejected with a ValidationException.
  • Compliance Status: If a record is created without any custom metadata, AWS Agent Registry saves it as NON_COMPLIANT. Calling GetRegistryRecord returns the record’s custom metadata values and its compliance status.

🧩 Supported Fields and Enrichment

Organizations can use custom metadata fields to track ownership, environments, and compliance. Examples of these fields include:

  • Environment & Ownership: Fields such as environment (prod, staging, or dev), businessUnit, ownerTeam, supportContact, and costCenter record where a resource runs, who is responsible for it, and who pays for it.
  • Inventory Integration: A configuration management database (CMDB) ID links the record to an existing inventory, and a support-tier field sets expectations for dependents.
  • Security & Compliance: Fields such as data classification, compliance scope (like PCI or HIPAA), risk tier, scan status, and a scan report URL turn approvals into reviews of structured evidence. Existing scanners, CMDB sync jobs, and classification tools can write these values through the API before a record is submitted.

🔍 Discovery and Filtering

Custom metadata values are indexed for search. Approvers can use the validated values when reviewing records, and consumers and agents can use Discovery APIs to filter records based on custom attributes.

For example, a consumer or agent can combine a natural-language query with specific metadata filters, such as:

1

environment=prod AND businessUnit=payments AND securityScanStatus=PASSED

To ensure security, only approved records are returned; a record that matches the filters but has not been approved is omitted from the results.

As a use case, AnyCompany operates anycompany-governed-registry without auto-approval. Its payments team publishes an MCP record, payments-ledger-mcp (a read-only server for ledger lookups). Existing security and inventory systems enrich this MCP record before an approval function determines whether consumers can discover it.

🚀 Prerequisites

To get started with custom metadata schemas, you need:

  • An AWS account in a supported AWS Region.
  • Python 3.11 or later.
  • boto3 1.43.113 or later.

#AWSAgentRegistry #CloudGovernance #MetadataSchemas #CloudSecurity

Source: Govern and discover records with common metadata in AWS Agent Registry | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Amazon SageMaker AI Managed MLflow Now Supports Cross-Account Governance Topologies
item.description:
Amazon SageMaker AI Managed MLflow Now Supports Cross-Account Governance Topologies

Amazon SageMaker AI has expanded the capabilities of managed MLflow to support cross-account governance. This update allows larger organizations to separate development and production environments at the account level while maintaining a central governance function through two distinct topologies.

🧩 Architecture Topologies

Organizations can now implement cross-account governance using two primary patterns:

  • Hub-and-Spoke Pattern: This model centralizes governance by sharing a single MLflow app from a hub account across multiple development (spoke) accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
  • Hybrid Pattern: Designed for regulated environments, this pattern keeps development accounts fully isolated from the governance hub, requiring model owners to approve models locally before they are promoted to the central hub.

⚙️ Key Details

The system utilizes AWS RAM to share the MLflow app, enabling it to work even when accounts are not within the same organization by using external principals.

Role Environment/Tooling Responsibility
Data Scientist Jupyter notebook Registers models against the shared MLflow app from a spoke account
Governance Officer Amazon SageMaker Studio Models UI Validates synced metrics and lineage; approves models centrally
Administrator Console or CLI Performs one-time setup of RAM shares, bucket policies, and destination groups
ML Engineer CI/CD pipeline Deploys approved models to Amazon SageMaker endpoints in the spoke account

🔄 Implementation and Workflow

The technical setup requires configuring named AWS CLI profiles for both the spoke and hub accounts. A CloudFormation template provisions the necessary SageMaker AI Studio domain, user profile, and Managed MLflow app with AutoModelRegistrationEnabled.

When a data scientist in a spoke account registers a model, a Model Package Group and version are created synchronously in the hub account. To facilitate deployment, the hub attaches a resource policy to the group and shares it back to the spoke with AllowDeploy permissions. Model artifacts are stored in the hub account’s S3 bucket, with bucket policies granting the spoke account necessary permissions for artifact access during deployment.

🚀 Availability

Administrators can configure these topologies using the AWS Management Console or CLI. Working notebooks for these cross-account governance implementations are available in the accompanying GitHub repository.

#SageMaker #MLflow #AWS #MLOps #CloudGovernance

Source: Govern models with MLflow and Amazon SageMaker AI Model Registry sync: Part 2 | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AWS Agent Registry Generally Available for Enterprise AI Management
item.description:
AWS Agent Registry Generally Available for Enterprise AI Management

AWS has announced the general availability of the AWS Agent Registry, a service designed to provide a central, searchable catalog for agents, tools, skills, and custom resources. As organizations scale their use of agentic AI, they frequently face challenges including duplicative effort, version drift, and a lack of audit trails for distributed systems.

🔍 Overview

AWS Agent Registry addresses three primary challenges encountered by organizations scaling AI systems:

  • No authoritative inventory: Teams lack a single record of what exists, who owns it, or its maintenance status.
  • No cross-team discovery: Developers often rebuild existing capabilities because they cannot find tools built by other teams.
  • No governance or audit trail: There is no central way to track access, security reviews, or technical lineage.

🧩 How it works

The system is split into two distinct planes to separate administrative control from developer consumption:

The Governance Plane

This serves as the authoritative store for all registered resources. Admins use this plane to configure:

  • Compliance and security signals: Tracking whether a resource has passed security reviews or meets regulatory requirements.
  • Discovery policies: Entitlement-based search rules defining which teams can access specific resources.
  • Custom metadata schemas: Standardizing resource descriptions with fields like cost center, data classification, and SLA tier.

The Discovery Plane

This is the high-performance interface for consumers. It features:

  • Curated access: Shows only resources that have passed an organization’s approval bar.
  • Semantic and lexical search: Allows users to find resources by intent, such as searching for tools by task.
  • Trust signals: Surfaces summarized compliance information to help developers make informed usage decisions.

⚙️ Key details

The registry supports four specific types of records to maintain organizational standards:

Record Type Description
MCP Model Context Protocol server, its tools, resources, and prompts
Agent Agent2Agent (A2A) agent card defining agents and their skills
Skill Agent skill definitions in markdown files and associated code/packages
Custom Custom descriptor which must be valid JSON

💡 Why it matters

Organizations across various industries use the registry to move faster and reduce redundancy. Sony utilizes the registry to reuse agent patterns across business units, while Mitsubishi Electric is implementing it to provide developers with a single, trusted source for building new capabilities. Southwest utilizes the registry to prevent sprawl and scale enterprise innovation with confidence.

#AWS #AIAgents #CloudGovernance #EnterpriseAI

Source: Manage agents, tools and skills at scale with AWS Agent Registry | Amazon Web Services

item.title: 🌊 Navigate the FinOps Wave: Your Ultimate Guide to AWS at FinOps X 2025
item.description:
🌊 Navigate the FinOps Wave: Your Ultimate Guide to AWS at FinOps X 2025

📌 Summary

Mark your calendars for an unmissable opportunity! This guide walks you through all the exciting AWS activities at FinOps X 2025 in San Diego (June 2-5). From executive keynotes to hands-on optimization workshops and exclusive networking events, discover how to maximize your conference experience while connecting with AWS experts to elevate your cloud financial management journey.

🎯 Why FinOps X 2025 Matters for AWS Users

The convergence of cloud financial management and technological innovation has never been more critical than now. As organizations worldwide grapple with optimizing their cloud spend while maximizing value, FinOps X 2025 emerges as the premier gathering for practitioners seeking to master this balance.

If you’re leveraging AWS and want to enhance your cloud financial management strategy, this year’s conference in San Diego (June 2-5) offers unique opportunities to connect directly with AWS teams, discover cutting-edge optimization techniques, and network with industry leaders who’ve successfully navigated similar challenges.

📸 Imagine the San Diego waterfront setting where cloud financial experts will gather next month

🗓️ Your Day-by-Day AWS Experience Planner

𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝟬: 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗮𝘆, 𝗝𝘂𝗻𝗲 𝟮

Start your conference journey with two essential touchpoints:

  • AWS Booth Experience (4:00PM – 7:00PM) Connect with the OPTICS team and Cloud Financial Management experts to discuss your specific challenges and learn about the latest developments.

  • 🍹 AWS Reception Party (6:30-8:30PM, Coronado Terrace) Network in style at this exclusive social mixer! Enjoy refreshments and meaningful conversations with AWS team members and fellow FinOps leaders in a relaxed atmosphere. This is your chance to establish connections before the formal sessions begin.

Pro tip: Don’t forget to RSVP for the reception to secure your spot!

𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝟭: 𝗧𝘂𝗲𝘀𝗱𝗮𝘆, 𝗝𝘂𝗻𝗲 𝟯

Your day begins with industry-leading insights:

  • Leadership Keynote (8:00-9:30AM, Keynote Stage) Don’t miss James Greenfield, VP of AWS Commerce Platform, participating in a high-level panel discussion with cloud industry leaders.

  • 𝙎𝙩𝙖𝙣𝙙𝙤𝙪𝙩 𝙎𝙚𝙨𝙨𝙞𝙤𝙣𝙨:

    1. Lockheed Martin’s 30% Cost Savings Story (11:00-11:45AM) Learn how this aerospace giant achieved remarkable cost efficiency through advanced FinOps practices.

    2. 🔥 The Frugality Fest Workshop (1:00-3:00PM) Form a team and compete in real-time cost optimization challenges! Bring your laptop for this hands-on experience with a pre-populated AWS account.

    3. Adapting FinOps for Generative AI (4:15-5:00PM) Discover how traditional CFM practices can be leveraged while addressing the unique cost considerations of GenAI workloads.

𝗗𝗮𝘆 𝟮: 𝗪𝗲𝗱𝗻𝗲𝘀𝗱𝗮𝘆, 𝗝𝘂𝗻𝗲 𝟰

The innovation continues:

  • Leadership Keynote (8:00-9:30AM, Keynote Stage) John Phillips, Director of AWS Insights and Optimization, will unveil exciting new announcements you won’t want to miss.

  • 𝙏𝙚𝙘𝙝𝙣𝙞𝙘𝙖𝙡 𝙄𝙢𝙢𝙚𝙧𝙨𝙞𝙤𝙣:

    1. What’s New in Cost Optimization (11:00-11:45AM) Get the latest on AWS cost optimization capabilities for monitoring performance, costs, and receiving actionable recommendations.

    2. 🧮 Advanced CUR Analytics (1:00-2:00PM) Master the art of querying AWS Cost and Usage Reports for deeper insights into service usage and optimization opportunities.

    3. New AWS FinOps Tools Revealed (4:15-5:00PM) Explore recent enhancements designed to transform cost analysis workflows, improve estimation accuracy, and strengthen governance.

📸 Visualize the AWS Stage room where these in-depth technical sessions will take place

🤝 Make Meaningful Connections

Beyond scheduled sessions, FinOps X 2025 offers valuable opportunities for personalized engagement:

  • One-on-One Meetings: Connect with AWS Cloud Financial Management product leaders to discuss your specific challenges and provide direct feedback that shapes future offerings.

  • AWS Booth Consultations: Available throughout Tuesday and Wednesday (7:00AM – 5:00PM), the booth serves as your hub for impromptu discussions with AWS experts who love “getting nerdy about FinOps.”

  • Group Discussions: Coordinate with your account team to join focused conversations around particular aspects of cloud financial management.

🚀 Why This Matters: Beyond Just Another Conference

FinOps X 2025 represents more than just technical sessions—it’s a strategic opportunity to reshape your organization’s approach to cloud economics. With AWS showcasing new tools while featuring customer success stories like Lockheed Martin’s impressive 30% savings implementation, attendees gain practical frameworks they can apply immediately.

The emphasis on hands-on experiences—particularly the Frugality Fest Workshop—demonstrates AWS’s commitment to practical skill development rather than theoretical concepts alone. Additionally, the forward-looking sessions on Generative AI cost management highlight how FinOps practices must evolve alongside emerging technologies.

For organizations struggling to balance innovation with fiscal responsibility, these sessions provide the ideal blend of strategic vision and tactical implementation guidance from those who’ve successfully navigated these waters.

💭 Final Thoughts: Maximizing Your FinOps X Investment

The convergence of financial and technical expertise represented at FinOps X 2025 creates a unique learning environment. By strategically planning your schedule to include AWS keynotes, practical workshops, and networking opportunities, you position yourself to bring transformative insights back to your organization.

As cloud technologies continue evolving at breakneck speeds, will your organization’s financial governance keep pace? FinOps X 2025 might just provide the blueprint you need.
